meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

events.title: Beaver Bauer: From Street to Stage, A Fifty-Year Retrospective
events.note: Fifty years of costume design — most of it for the Pickle Family Circus and A.C.T. — free in the Main Library's sixth-floor gallery.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Nine to ten on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays the 1894 garden is free to everybody; San Francisco residents are free any time with ID. The hour before the crowds is the one worth taking.

events.title: Graciela Iturbide: Between Two Worlds
events.note: A major retrospective of the Mexican photographer whose Juchitán pictures changed how the isthmus was seen. The best photography show in the city.

events.title: Ha Chong-Hyun: Retrospective
events.note: Sixty years of the Korean Dansaekhwa painter who pushed paint through the back of the canvas. Ten till five.

events.title: Safeway Holiday Ice Rink opens in Union Square
events.note: The rink is up in Union Square for the season, ten till eleven daily. Free to look at, skating extra, and genuinely good at dusk.

events.title: Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean
events.note: Vishnu across a thousand years of South and Southeast Asian art, from temple bronzes to painted manuscripts.

events.title: Market/Value
events.venue: Thacher Gallery, University of San Francisco
events.note: A free university show on markets and what they measure. Noon till six.

events.title: BROKEN VEIN
events.note: A run of three screenings a day in the Presidio's small Chestnut Street house. Descriptor is lower-confidence — the listing carries the times and nothing about the film.

events.title: French Café Music with Bistro Moustache
events.note: Accordion-and-guitar musette over dinner on California Street — the real repertoire, not a theme night. Free with an RSVP.

events.title: Fatherland
events.note: In the Roxie's rotating autumn run, playing twice most days this week. Descriptor is lower-confidence — the calendar gives the time and the poster.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Documentary assembled from night-time rooftop conversations in Tel Aviv about the machinery behind Israel's mass targeting. Third week at the Roxie.

events.title: Cyberpunk Cinema Night
events.note: Free cyberpunk screenings in the back of the Knockout, half six. One of the free nights DICE does not carry, which is why sources.yml says to read Funcheap too.

events.title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: Classes plus Salsa and Bachata Dancing
events.note: A beginners' class at half six and five hours of social dancing after it. The city's most durable Monday dance night, in a Richmond room that does nothing else as well.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: Free with an Eventbrite RSVP, $20–$25 at the door, two-drink minimum. The Function books better comics than a free Monday has any right to.

events.title: Intro to Personal Safety and Self-Defense
events.note: An hour of free instruction in the back of a sporting-goods shop. RSVP required and it fills.

events.title: Karaoke: NightZ @ Z
events.note: The Mission's experimental theatre opens its bar and its sound system for karaoke. Free with RSVP, and a chance to see the inside of Z Space for nothing.

events.title: Motown on Mondays
events.note: Fifteen years of 45s on a Monday — Motown, Stax and the northern-soul end of it, all vinyl. Free before eight, $5 after, still the cheapest dancing in the city.

events.title: Sharks vs Islanders: Native American Heritage Celebration
events.note: The Islanders in on a Monday, with the Sharks' Native American Heritage night around it. Weeknight upper-bowl seats stay cheap and Diridon is ten minutes' walk.

events.title: Town Biz Comedy Night
events.note: HellaFunny's Monday night in Temescal, free with RSVP, with mezcal and mole to buy. It runs Mondays and Tuesdays and Monday is the looser bill.

events.title: Warriors vs Pelicans
events.note: Arena basketball, listed for completeness — findable without this digest's help. New Orleans in on a Monday.

events.title: Comedy at The Freight
events.note: Stand-up in a seated listening room, which changes the comedy more than you would think. Sliding scale from $10.

events.title: A Tribute to Grover Washington Jr.
events.note: Kevin Moore, Angelo Luster, Ashley Jemison and Eldon T. Jones on the soprano-sax songbook that made smooth jazz respectable before the term existed. Mister Magic played straight.

events.title: Donavon Frankenreiter & The Band of Heathens
events.note: Surf-bred barroom soul from Frankenreiter and Austin's most reliable roots-rock band on a double bill. Doors seven. Four minutes' walk from Caltrain Menlo Park, which is how to do it.

events.title: Fjord
events.note: A title in the Roxie's rotating run. The calendar gives the time and the poster and nothing else; descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: Mirthquake: Monday Live Comedy
events.note: Free with RSVP in an Irish bar on Geary, $5 drinks, and a room small enough that the comics can hear you not laughing. 21+.

events.title: Past Self with Creux Lies and Hot Goth GF
events.note: Three bands deep into the darkwave revival — cold synths, chorus-drenched guitar and a Sacramento headliner who takes it seriously. All ages.

events.title: Quadeca: Life 1 Tour
events.note: A YouTube rapper who turned into a genuinely strange art-pop producer. DerbyOlēka opens. The Fillmore's own listing gives no time; eight is the house's usual.

events.title: Sienna Spiro: My House Tour with Summer Joy
events.note: A young British singer with a big, unhurried voice, in a 1,400-seat picture palace on a Monday. Sold out, and already rebooked into the Greek for next September.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: John Wilson's first feature after How To with John Wilson — the same accidental-encounter method at feature length, and much stranger for it. Holds over.

events.title: Weston Estate with Hojean
events.note: North Carolina bedroom R&B played by a six-piece who met in high school — the harmonies are the point. A second night added after the first sold; this is the extra one.

events.title: Hubba Hubba Revue presents Monday Night Hubba
events.note: Burlesque and variety in DNA's upstairs room, from the troupe that has run this city's best-dressed nonsense for two decades. Sourced from a sweep rather than the club's calendar.

events.title: Krazy for Karaoke
events.note: The Knockout's Monday karaoke, which is less a performance than a contact sport. Free on a DICE RSVP.

events.title: Death Guild
events.note: The longest-running goth-industrial night in the United States and the second-longest in the world, every Monday since 1993. Found on a listings sweep, not DNA's own calendar, which this run does not fetch.

events.title: Breadboarding Modular Synthesizers, Part II
events.note: The second half of Gray Area's hands-on synth-building workshop, in the Grand on Mission. No time published; the hall's workshops usually run early evening.

events.title: San Francisco Botanical Garden Free Day
events.note: Second Tuesday of the month, fifty-five acres in Golden Gate Park free to everyone. Open from half seven.

events.title: Fernando Carnaúba and Albert Dicruttalo: Momentum
events.note: Two sculptors on movement, free, nine till five.

events.title: Nostalgia
events.note: A group show in the SoMa gallery, free, nine till five.

events.title: No Punk. No Future.
events.note: German punk's first decade, in posters, fanzines and record sleeves, on the Goethe-Institut's walls. Free with RSVP, weekdays only.

events.title: Siddharth Parasnis: Conversation in Color
events.note: Thickly built architectural abstraction on Sutter Street, free.

events.title: Robert Adams: Contact
events.note: The photographer who made the American West look exactly as developed as it is. Half ten till half five, free.

events.title: Chuck Sperry: Archetypes
events.note: The Bay Area gig-poster printmaker's hand-pulled screenprints shown as the fine art they have quietly become. Free.

events.title: Chris Natrop
events.note: Hand-cut paper landscapes at architectural scale, in the Minnesota Street Project. Noon till four, free.

events.title: BROKEN VEIN
events.note: Three screenings a day continue. Descriptor withheld rather than guessed.

events.title: Being Heumann
events.note: The Judy Heumann documentary — the disability-rights organiser who made the 504 sit-in happen, told largely in her own voice. A mid-afternoon show.

events.title: Henry J. Evans: Bombs, Bacon, and Bankruptcy
events.note: An author evening at the Ferry Building shop, rescheduled from an earlier date. Free.

events.title: Haiti Scholarship Benefit
events.note: A fundraiser in the deconsecrated church on Tenth Street, which is worth the ticket for the room alone.

events.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
events.note: A Harlem story opening its Roxie run this week and playing most days. The house's main new title.

events.title: THX 1138 (35mm)
events.note: Lucas's first feature on a 35mm print — the cold, white, over-lit version of the future that almost no one copied. The format is the reason to go.

events.title: Yoga on the Labyrinth
events.note: An hour and a quarter of yoga on the cathedral's indoor labyrinth, under the vaulting, with live music. Strange and genuinely calming.

events.title: Conundrum Chronicles StorySlam
events.note: True stories told cold, ten minutes each, in the Marsh's Valencia Street room. $10 sliding scale.

events.title: Covenant
events.note: York Walker's Faustian blues play — a guitarist comes home too good, and the town draws its own conclusions. Still in previews; press night is Wednesday.

events.title: Entangled Intelligences
events.note: A performance evening at the Cowell about machine and human cognition sharing a stage. Fort Mason's big hall is renter-programmed, so this one is easy to miss.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Bess Wohl's Pulitzer-winning play about a 1970s consciousness-raising group, seen by the daughter of one of them. West Coast premiere, running to 29 November.

events.title: Live Model Tuesday Sketch
events.note: A life-drawing session in a bar, materials your own problem. One of the city's oldest standing Tuesday fixtures and still free.

events.title: Mezcal and Mole Comedy Night
events.note: The Tuesday half of HellaFunny's Temescal residency — a tighter bill than Monday's. Free with RSVP.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: The Mischief company's Peter Pan, in which everything that can fall down does. Running to 28 November; tickets from $55.

events.title: Sparta with Public Opinion
events.note: Jim Ward's band after At the Drive-In — tighter, less frantic, and still capable of the same wall of noise. The South Bay gets the first of two Bay Area nights.

events.title: Claudio Simonetti's Goblin performs the live score to Tenebre
events.note: Goblin playing their own Argento score against the film, under the Castro's ceiling. The prog-horror synth canon performed by the man who wrote it — doors at half six.

events.title: Hélène Grimaud
events.note: One of the most individual pianists working, in Davies on a Tuesday. The Songkick calendar this project uses for the hall shows nothing before 24 November — between September and June a blank week there means nothing.

events.title: Las Lomas High School
events.note: A Walnut Creek high-school jazz band on a professional stage, which is how the Bay Area's jazz programmes have always worked. $30.

events.title: The Marriage of Figaro
events.note: San Francisco Opera's Figaro, the third of eight performances in a run to 29 November. Three and a half hours of Mozart's best-built comedy.

events.title: Buzzcocks and Modern English with Grade 2
events.note: Fifty years of Buzzcocks on a co-headline with Modern English, and Grade 2 — the Isle of Wight's best current punk band — opening. First of two nights and the one with tickets left.

events.title: Ken Russell's The Devils (4K restoration)
events.note: The film Warner Bros. spent fifty years trying to bury, restored. Russell at his most unhinged and Oliver Reed at his best. Not a date film.

events.title: Rio Amor and Friends
events.note: A local songwriter calling in favours on the Great American's stage. Doors seven, and the guest list is the reason to go.

events.title: Weston Estate with Hojean
events.note: The original night, which sold before the Monday show was added. Same bill, fuller room.

events.title: Yuki Chiba: First North America Headline Tour
events.note: The Japanese rapper formerly known as KOHH, whose verse on Team Tomodachi put him in front of a Western audience. First headline run on this continent.

events.title: Fatherland
events.note: Second showing of the day in the Roxie's rotating run. Descriptor is lower-confidence.

events.title: $6 Drive-In Movie Night
events.note: Six dollars a head at a surviving twin drive-in, every Tuesday. Two dollars for children. Bring a blanket; the East Bay gets cold by the second feature.

events.title: Hit The Lights with Forever Came Calling and Fox Royale
events.note: Ohio pop-punk that never pretended to grow out of it, three bands deep, 21+. Music at half eight in a room that closes for good at the end of 2026.

events.title: Death TKO: Darkwave Dance Party with DJ Audrey and DJ Paul Costuros
events.note: Minimal synth, cold wave and the bleaker end of post-punk, played by two DJs with genuinely deep crates. Free on a DICE RSVP.

events.title: Kilowatt Karaoke
events.note: Tuesday karaoke in a 150-cap Mission bar, free on a DICE RSVP. The song list skews to things nobody should attempt.

events.title: Multi-City Live Theater in VR with Ferryman Collective
events.note: Ferryman Collective's live performance played simultaneously across cities in virtual reality, hosted in the Grand. No time published.

events.title: Teddy Swims with MarcLo
events.note: Arena soul-pop, listed for completeness — the brief deprioritises arenas and this needs no help being found.

events.title: The Tallest Man On Earth
events.note: Kristian Matsson alone with a guitar in the Palace's 950-seat hall, which is the right room for a voice that carries that far. Time unconfirmed.

events.title: Free National Parks Day: Muir Woods and the Hyde Street Pier ships
events.note: Veterans Day waives entrance fees across the national parks — the Hyde Street Pier fleet in the city, Muir Woods across the bridge. Muir Woods still needs a paid parking or shuttle reservation, so book before you drive.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The Monday–Wednesday–Friday free hour, nine till ten. On a holiday Wednesday it will be busier than usual.

events.title: Miró: Proof Against All
events.note: Miró's work from the war and the years after, when he went back to printmaking because materials were short. Free for Bay Area residents on Saturday.

events.title: Awaking Beauty: The Art of Eyvind Earle
events.note: The background painter who gave Sleeping Beauty its tapestry verticals, shown properly for once. Ten till half five.

events.title: USS Hornet Veterans Day
events.venue: USS Hornet Sea, Air and Space Museum
events.note: Veterans Day aboard an Essex-class carrier that recovered Apollo 11 and 12. Ten till five, and the hangar deck is the draw.

events.title: Free Admission Day at Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Galleries free every Wednesday, eleven till eight. Dread Scott's The Body Politic and Rael San Fratello's Prototypes and Provocations are both up, and both repay the hour.

events.title: Syd Mead: Future Pastime
events.note: The concept artist who designed Blade Runner's Los Angeles and Tron's grid, in the Transamerica's ground-floor space. Free, and it closes soon.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Maren Hassinger, Living Moving Growing
events.note: A free-with-admission lunchtime walk through the Hassinger retrospective — fifty years of wire rope, branches and plastic bags made to behave like bodies.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: A Wednesday matinee of the Mischief company's collapsing Peter Pan. The Playhouse publishes no per-date schedule; this is its standing weekly pattern.

events.title: BROKEN VEIN
events.note: Three screenings a day, 3.20, 5.40 and 8.

events.title: Marcus Thompson II: Game Changers
events.note: The Athletic's Warriors writer on the book. Free at the Ferry Building shop.

events.title: Rock Ross: Go Like This (16mm)
events.note: Canyon Cinema presents Rock Ross on 16mm with the filmmaker in the room for questions. The Bay Area experimental-film lineage, shown the way it was shot.

events.title: Holy Wave and Queen Serene
events.note: Austin psych that has slowed down into something closer to dub than garage, in a 150-cap Mission bar. One of the better small bookings of the week.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Second of the week's eight Liberation performances.

events.title: Monthly Trivia Night
events.note: Free trivia in the Divisadero bar, monthly rather than weekly, which keeps the questions fresh.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Wednesday evening, seven o'clock.

events.title: Samurai Rebellion
events.note: Kobayashi's 1967 film with Toshiro Mifune as a retainer who finally refuses. In BAMPFA's Masaki Kobayashi retrospective — the best repertory series running in the Bay Area right now.

events.title: Sharks vs Penguins: Military Appreciation
events.note: Pittsburgh in on Veterans Day, with the Sharks' military night around it. The best-value hockey ticket of the three this week.

events.title: Dear San Francisco
events.note: The 7 Fingers' acrobatic love letter to the city, in the room Beach Blanket Babylon ran in for forty-five years. Still the best thing in North Beach.

events.title: Herlin Riley
events.note: New Orleans drumming in the direct line — Riley played with Wynton Marsalis for a decade and carries the second-line feel into straight-ahead jazz without flattening either.

events.title: Open Mic at the San Jose Improv
events.note: The Improv's open mic on the main stage, which is a bigger room than an open mic deserves and makes it more interesting to watch.

events.title: Philharmonia Baroque: Handel's The Power of Music
events.note: Peter Whelan conducts Handel's 1742 Dublin version of Alexander's Feast, with Sherezade Panthaki, Rachael Wilson and James Way. First of three nights across three counties; from $40, $20 under thirty.

events.title: Punch Line Secret Guest List
events.note: Free with RSVP at the Battery Street club, which means a surprise bill and sometimes a very big name working out material. 18+, two-drink minimum, arrive half an hour early.

events.title: Will Bernard and Beth Custer
events.note: Guitar and clarinet in a Glen Park bookshop that has run live jazz for decades. Bernard's playing is the Bay Area's quiet connective tissue.

events.title: Arab Film Festival: Chronicle of a Disappearance
events.note: Elia Suleiman's 1996 debut — deadpan, static-framed, and the template for everything he made after. In the 30th Arab Film Festival. From $20.

events.title: Aterciopelados: La Pipa de La Paz 30th Anniversary
events.note: Andrea Echeverri and Héctor Buitrago playing the record that made Colombian rock a going concern, thirty years on. Edú Bega opens. Sold out.

events.title: Buzzcocks and Modern English with Grade 2
events.note: The second of two nights. If you can only take one, Tuesday is the one with tickets; this is the one with the better-warmed room.

events.title: Fruit Looops with Fee Faw Fum, Arts & Crafts and Beatcuntz
events.note: Four bands from the loud, funny, deliberately unserious end of the Midwest-to-Mission pipeline. Ohio headliners in a bar that fits 150.

events.title: Jake Xerxes Fussell with Dougie Poole
events.note: Fussell sings other people's old songs — ballads, work songs, fragments — with a guitar touch that makes them sound found rather than revived. Dougie Poole's cosmic country underneath. Doors seven.

events.title: Mad Tsai with Piao and bluhour
events.note: Bedroom pop with a bisexual-anthem streak and a crowd that sings every word. Michael Cimino's bluhour opens. All ages.

events.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
events.note: Second night of the Roxie's new Harlem title.

events.title: Roosters Comedy Showcase
events.note: The Sunnyvale club's own Wednesday showcase — six or seven comics working out material before the weekend headliner arrives. Two-item minimum.

events.title: Soft Cell
events.note: Marc Almond and Dave Ball on what is billed as a farewell run. Tainted Love is the least interesting thing they did and the Danceteria set knows it.

events.title: Sparta
events.note: The second Bay Area night, in a 400-cap room — the better of the two if you want to be close to it.

events.title: Stop Light Observations with Runner and Bobby
events.note: Charleston rock with a gospel-choir streak and a live show that does not sound like the records. Eight o'clock.

events.title: The Damned: Final Damnation 50
events.note: Fifty years of the first British punk band to put out a single, with the Flamin' Groovies — a San Francisco institution older still — and Denmark's Courettes. The best bill in the city tonight.

events.title: Ólafur Arnalds
events.note: Icelandic minimalism for piano, strings and two self-playing pianos of his own design. A second show added after the first sold; both are gone.

events.title: lowercase with Shearling and Wife
events.note: The 1990s slowcore band whose records were mostly silence and then suddenly not. All ages, $15 advance, and cheap for what it is.

events.title: Downtown 81 Mutant Disco Dance Party
events.note: No wave, mutant disco and the ZE Records catalogue — the sound of New York between punk and house. Free on a DICE RSVP.

events.title: Italo Frisco
events.note: Italo disco on vinyl — the overblown, arpeggiated, entirely sincere Italian version of synth-pop. No cover published.

events.title: 8TURN 2ND WORLD TOUR: 8TURN TRACE
events.note: A K-pop boy group's second world tour, in Redwood City of all places. The Fox sells no tickets for it and publishes no time or room — a promoter date, so confirm before travelling.

events.title: Bob Marley: How Reggae Changed the World
events.note: Duane Forrest's performance-lecture on how one Jamaican catalogue reorganised global pop, running in the Bing's small studio through Sunday. No times published.

events.title: Brand New
events.note: Jesse Lacey's band, back on the road after the long silence, in a 7,000-capacity hall. Deja Entendu is the reason the room will be full.

events.title: Modele
events.note: A booking in Albany's 150-cap room, which books better than its size suggests. Lineup details are thin — the Ivy Room's own calendar does not fetch and this comes from a mirror.

events.title: Patch Bay: Render Settings, with Mikey J and Ratha Nou
events.note: Gray Area's monthly creative-technology meetup, this one on rendering. No time published; the series usually runs from seven.

events.title: Invaders: Vallejo, Food and the Making of California
events.note: Mariano Vallejo, his ranchos and the agricultural order they imposed, told through food. Eleven till six.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: A one o'clock matinee, the cheapest Liberation of the week at $70.

events.title: BROKEN VEIN
events.note: Last of the four listed days.

events.title: Sip and Sketch: Eyvind Earle-Inspired Scratchboards
events.note: Scratchboard work after hours in the Presidio, keyed to the Earle exhibition — the background painter who gave Sleeping Beauty its verticals.

events.title: Chronotope Opening Reception
events.note: An opening on Minna Street with the artists in the room. Free, six till eight.

events.title: Kim Shuck's Poem Jam celebrates Janice Gould's This Music
events.note: A former San Francisco poet laureate convening a reading for the late Koyangk'auwi Maidu poet Janice Gould. Free, in the Main Library's Latino Room.

events.title: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
events.note: Miyazaki before Ghibli existed, in Japantown's basement cinema. The one where the ecological argument is least sentimental.

events.title: Panel: Mother Jones, 50 Years of Fearless Journalism
events.note: Half a century of the magazine, discussed by the people who made it. Free in the Koret.

events.title: SF State Free Rooftop Stargazing
events.note: The top floor of Thornton Hall, a large telescope and someone who knows how to point it. Free and weather-dependent, which in November means check first.

events.title: Band of Outsiders
events.note: Godard's 1964 heist-that-isn't, with the Louvre run and the Madison. In BAMPFA's Godard early-films series, alongside the Gvido Augusts poster show.

events.title: Flight Club: Adult Flight Night
events.note: A trampoline park cleared of children for two hours. $20 an hour, grip socks compulsory, 18+. Filed under oddities and earning it.

events.title: Kitten on The Keys
events.note: Suzanne Ramsey's cabaret piano — Weimar by way of the Mission, filthy and technically excellent. No cover published.

events.title: Ockham with Ex Deus Machina, Splendor and Kevito Y Los Bravos
events.note: Four local bands across metal, post-hardcore and whatever Kevito Y Los Bravos are doing. Five dollars' worth of range for whatever the door is.

events.title: POC Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP in Temescal, an hour and a half, and a better bill than most paid rooms.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Thursday, seven o'clock.

events.title: Points of Departure, Fall 2026
events.note: Fort Mason's recurring contemporary-dance showcase, an evening of short works by companies who do not otherwise share a bill.

events.title: San Francisco Transgender Film Festival: Comedy
events.note: The 29th SFTFF, the oldest transgender film festival anywhere, opens with the comedy shorts. Sliding scale from $5. Three nights, six programmes.

events.title: Volti Vocal Ensemble with SFSU and SOTA
events.venue: Knuth Hall, San Francisco State University
events.note: Volti sings new choral music almost exclusively, and here they share a programme with two student choirs. Free, which for a group of this standard is unusual.

events.title: Arab Film Festival Under the Stars: Spices and Lies
events.note: A free outdoor screening in the Hayes Valley lot, RSVP required. Dress for a November night in a wind tunnel.

events.title: Comedy Sharks Standup Night
events.note: Free stand-up in a Half Moon Bay brewery, which is as close as the coast gets to a comedy club.

events.title: Dear San Francisco
events.note: The 7 Fingers' acrobatic city portrait, nightly in North Beach.

events.title: George Rogers Quartet
events.note: Thursday jazz among the shelves in Glen Park.

events.title: HellaFunny Thursday Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP downtown, $20–$25 at the door, two-drink minimum.

events.title: Jackiem Joyner
events.note: Contemporary saxophone with a harder R&B spine than the format usually allows. $29–$69.

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.note: Kimberly Belflower's play about a Georgia high-school English class reading The Crucible in 2018. First preview; the run goes to 13 December.

events.title: The Smithereens
events.note: Power pop from New Jersey with Marshall Crenshaw out front since Pat DiNizio died. A Girl Like You in a 300-seat theatre on a Saratoga hillside beats the same band in a shed.

events.title: Turnover with Nothing and Trauma Ray
events.note: Virginia emo that turned into dream pop and kept the audience. Nothing's shoegaze is the heavier half of the bill. Sold out; doors half six.

events.title: Band of Horses
events.note: Ben Bridwell's falsetto and the big reverb, twenty years on from Everything All the Time. The Regency is the right size for it.

events.title: Covenant
events.note: The first performance after Wednesday's press night.

events.title: Gene with Weston Loney
events.note: The Britpop-era band most often filed next to the Smiths and least deserving of it — Martin Rossiter's voice is the whole argument. Rare American date.

events.title: Isaiah Rashad: Lil Sunny's Awful Road Trip
events.note: The Chattanooga rapper whose records arrive rarely and land hard. Doors seven. Transit for this one — downtown Oakland garages shut their gates at seven on weeknights.

events.title: Jake Minch with Alix Page
events.note: Quiet, close-miked songwriting that came up on short video and translates better than it should to a room. $20–$25.

events.title: Joe Machi
events.note: The deadpan, oddly-pitched delivery that made him on Last Comic Standing, with David Nguyen and Jonny Stein. First of four nights in Sunnyvale.

events.title: Juan Atkins Forever: Free Tribute Party
events.note: A free night for the man who invented Detroit techno — Model 500, Cybotron, the lot. Doors eight, 21+, no cover. The best free music in the city this week.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Thursday evening performance.

events.title: Lissie with Harber Wynn
events.note: Iowa-raised songwriting that got better when it stopped chasing radio. Doors seven, and the Guild is a four-minute walk from Caltrain.

events.title: Marc Broussard with Cristina Vane
events.note: Louisiana blue-eyed soul with a real Bayou rhythm section behind it. Cristina Vane's slide playing is worth arriving for. Doors seven.

events.title: Natanya
events.note: Sold out at Brick & Mortar. Descriptor is lower-confidence — the listing is a name and a time.

events.title: Roger Clyne & PH Naffah
